start: Getting started with VBAi
You know VBA and your development environment. This guide explains how to use the commands, windows and safeguards specific to VBAi.
Getting started
Help
VBAi
The walkthrough used in this guide

The walkthrough starts with a new Excel workbook, CalculTVA.xlsm. We choose Codex with the Luna model and medium reasoning, ask for a window to calculate a tax-inclusive amount, then add and run tests in separate exchanges. We then publish the sources on a dedicated GitHub branch.
Excel is the host here. Project selection, chat, the editor and synchronization use the shared VBE layer; host-specific commands remain subject to that host’s capabilities.
Panel detail after creating the CalculTVA project: the selected document appears above the welcome screen.
The selected document determines the working project.
Prepare your workspace
Create a document in the host application, then save it in a format that preserves the VBA project. VBAi associates conversations and the repository with this document’s path.
Open the VBE. Under View, open the VBAi panel; under Tools, open its settings. If these commands are missing, check that the add-in is loaded in the VBE Add-In Manager.
Configure the provider, then return to the chat. The project selector at the top of the panel must identify the document you want to work on.
Click the model name below the input box to show the provider, model and, where supported, reasoning selectors.
Choose your next action
Your goal
What to read
Send your first request
Configure connections, then Request a change
Have the agent work on existing code
Attach the right context
Check what it changed
Review and undo a change
Track modules in GitHub
Link the document to a repository, then Source conversion
Find a conversation
Resume a conversation
Open the guide from the VBE

In the VBE’s “?” or Help menu, choose VBAi · User guide. The same guide is available in About VBAi. It opens in the interface language; if the corresponding local file is missing, VBAi tries English, then French. The compiled files must be in the Help folder beside the application.
settings: Configure connections
Settings establish the connections. Choose the model for a request in the conversation.
Provider
Codex
API key
Ollama
GitHub Copilot
Settings
Open settings

Use Tools > VBAi Configuration in the VBE, or Settings in the chat’s … menu. The Provider page displays only settings relevant to the chosen connection: account authentication, API key or service address. Switching providers should not require you to fill in another provider’s fields.

In the illustrated walkthrough, we use Codex with the account connection offered by VBAi. The Luna model and medium level are then selected in the chat. For Ollama, enter your service’s address and check that the desired model is available there; saving an address does not download a model.
Active Codex connection: set the model and reasoning in the conversation.
Validate the connection in the chat
Save the settings and return to the conversation.
Open the selector below the input box, then choose the provider. VBAi reloads its model catalog.
Select the model. Set the reasoning if a list of levels is offered; its absence may simply mean the model does not expose it.
If the catalog stays empty, use Refresh models in the … menu and read the status at the bottom of the panel. Correct the connection before resending your request.
Input area detail: Codex, GPT-6-Luna and medium selected.
Choose the provider, model and reasoning here.
Collapse the lists using the model summary.
Keep the two GitHub connections separate

The GitHub account on the dedicated page is used for repositories and pull requests. This choice is separate from GitHub Copilot as a conversation provider. Connecting one does not establish the other.

Default choices are preserved; a saved conversation also preserves its provider, model and reasoning choices. When resuming a history, check the name shown below the input box rather than assuming it uses the current default.
Find configuration from the VBE
Under Tools, VBAi Configuration opens connections and appearance. Update, reporting and About commands are grouped in the same place.
VBAi entries in the Tools menu.
appearance: Arrange windows and choose a theme
Adapt VBAi to your workspace through settings and VBE commands.
In settings, open Appearance and choose Light, Dark or System. This setting affects VBAi surfaces. Native editor colors and VBE docking preferences have their own state.
After a change, check lists, code differences and menus. If text becomes unreadable, return to the previous theme and note the affected window for your report.
Actual panel menu: settings, access, catalog, docking, GitHub and About.

The chat’s … menu offers switching between docked and floating. The VBE then manages the container’s position. For a side panel, place it on the desired edge using the VBE’s usual layout commands. Closing a panel does not uninstall the add-in: reopen it from View.
Monaco occupies the editor workspace. The conversation and Test Explorer remain separate windows. Monaco should not impose the docking choice for another window, such as the Object Browser.
The VBE View menu lets you reopen the VBAi Assistant, VBAi Editor, Test Explorer and GitHub window. Closing one of these windows does not uninstall the add-in.
VBAi commands in Excel’s View menu.
conversation: Request a change
Send a request from the chosen project, then follow its execution in the same panel.
Conversation
Model
Reasoning
Mode
Send
New conversation
Select the scope of work

The project shown at the top of the chat is the starting point for the agent’s tools. Check it before every new conversation, especially when several documents have similar names. On a new project, no module reference is needed to request an initial implementation.

The first request is deliberately simple: “I’d like a small window to enter an amount before tax and a VAT rate, then obtain the amount including tax. Can you prepare that for me?” The agent chooses the structure. The request for tests comes in a separate exchange after the initial implementation.
Choose the mode and send
Below the input box, choose Discussion for an explanation, Plan to prepare work, or Agent to authorize implementation within the approval policy’s limits.
Choose the model using the button bearing its name. Collapsing the selector does not change this choice.
Enter the request and use Send. Enter also sends; Shift+Enter inserts a line. When a suggestion is open, accepting it takes priority.
Read the activities during the response. The send button becomes Stop when the input box is empty and a turn is in progress.
Check completion

A final message is not proof that the project was changed. Open the reported modules and change cards, then compile and test. If the agent describes code or a JSON call without executing it, ask it to read the current state and apply the change with its tools. Do not blindly repeat a creation: the component may already exist.
The /expliquer, /corriger and /refactoriser commands prepare a request using the editor context. They do not remove the need to check the project and the scope of the change.
First work on the form. The change cards and project code let you verify what was applied.
context: VBAi can attach project references, selected code and local notes. The inspector lets you check what will be sent with the next request.

Type # to select a project or module, and @ to select a procedure. Choose the suggested entry instead of leaving an ambiguous name in the text. References become context items that you can open or remove.

For a localized change, attach the procedure and its relevant dependencies. The selection button adds the active VBE excerpt. From Monaco, an assistance action can attach the selected draft; distinguish this draft from code already present in the project.
Open outgoing context using the inspection button below the input box. Review the included project, references, excerpts and notes. Refresh rebuilds this preview after a context change.

The preview shows data prepared for the next message. It is not a complete copy of internal instructions or the provider’s entire protocol history. A file supplied by path remains separate context from the VBA project.

Remove a reference if it no longer relates to the request. If a module has been renamed or deleted since selection, choose the current reference again. Project and revision checks remain active when the agent calls a tool.
activity: Activities connect a request to observed operations. Expand them to understand an action or locate a failure.

Successive activities in the same intervention are grouped between messages. Expand the group, then a step, to read the tool name, its status and available details. A collapsed group reduces clutter without removing this information.
Reasoning · summary displays summaries sent by the provider. This section can remain empty if the provider does not produce any; it does not provide access to complete internal reasoning.

A successful read confirms that the tool returned data. A successful change must be checked against its change card and a fresh reading of the project. A failed or interrupted step may leave a partial state: read the details before retrying.
In CalculTVA, checking module contents is essential: creating modules does not guarantee that their code was inserted. An agent’s declarative response does not replace this check.

Use the return to the latest message if you scrolled up the history during streaming. Response buttons let you copy its content or continue from it, among other actions. Review project changes in their dedicated cards.
queue: Prepare a request during a response
The queue lets you prepare what comes next while distinguishing a new request from stopping the current turn.
Add a message to the queue

While the agent works, enter the next request and send it. With text in the input box, Send places this message in the queue; with an empty input box, the button stops the active turn. References and attachments are preserved with the queued request.

Each row offers editing, deletion or priority sending. Edit returns the request to the input box; delete removes only that queued item. Send now requests interruption of active work, then waits for cleanup before starting the chosen message.
An error, manual stop or budget pause should not silently start the entire queue. Review the agent’s status and message context before resuming.

The queue belongs to the conversation. It can reappear with its history, but its reappearance does not mean it was executed. If the project or its revision has changed, checks may leave the request queued.
history: Resume a conversation
The history button replaces the conversation in the chat’s central area. The list concerns the selected document.
History
Archive
Delete a conversation
Memory
Unsaved document
Open history, then return to the conversation

Click the history icon to the left of the project selector. The list occupies the full width of the central area; the transcript is hidden while you browse it. The same button becomes the return to the conversation. Your draft and current messages are preserved.
Selecting a conversation reloads its history, draft and model choices. Check the project and references again before continuing if the code has changed since that work.
The two CalculTVA conversations occupy the panel’s entire central area.
Conversations for the selected document.
Actions apply to the selected conversation.
Return to the chat while preserving the draft.
Organize conversations

Search narrows the displayed list. Enter a title in the dedicated field, then use Rename. Pin makes it easier to return to a conversation; archive removes it from the current list without deleting it. Show archived conversations to find it again.
Delete requests confirmation and removes the selected conversation from local history. Export Markdown produces a readable copy of the exchange; this file does not back up VBA modules.
Save the document and local notes
A macro that has never been saved uses a temporary session: it does not leave durable orphaned history if abandoned. The first save allows association with the saved document.

Document memory contains local notes that you write. Save locally preserves these notes. The checkbox for attaching them to the next request determines whether they are sent to the provider; it does not automatically grant access to other projects.
privacy: The project shown at the top of the chat is the target of changes. Set additional read access and confirmations before writing separately.

In the chat’s … menu, open project access. The linked project remains readable; check additional projects the agent needs to understand calls or dependencies. This read permission does not change the write target.
Applying a new scope starts a new conversation. Information already sent in the previous conversation cannot be withdrawn from the provider.
Choose when to confirm a change

The approval selector below the input box controls confirmations for VBA operations. In Automatic mode, eligible operations can proceed without a dialog for every change. Conversation mode, project protection and revision checks continue to apply.
When a dialog appears, review the project and action. Allow applies to this proposal; Deny blocks it. If an error reports an uncertain outcome, inspect the project before repeating the request.

Debugging windows and some VBE surfaces can contain information from several projects. Shared context and clipboard access are explicitly configured. Enable them for a task requiring this data; they do not grant permission to modify other projects.
The permission used for running tests includes shared VBE context and the clipboard. Applying it opens a new conversation.
Review the exact scope of this permission.
Apply the scope to a new conversation.
changes: Change cards let you review modifications associated with the conversation and choose exactly what to undo.
Open the change you want to inspect

From the card, open the comparison. Side-by-side mode shows Before and After; unified mode combines deletions and additions. Collapse context to isolate differences, then use the arrows to move between changes.

Open module navigates to the actual target if it still exists. This check is useful after several requests: an older comparison represents the change from its turn, while the module may have changed since.
Choose the scope of the undo
Undo block targets only part of the change. Undo change targets the relevant card; undo turn concerns changes associated with the agent’s turn. Available options depend on the change type.
VBAi checks revisions before writing. If you have changed code in the meantime, a refusal avoids overwriting that edit. Read the current content before deciding what to keep.
Undoing code does not automatically restore workbook data, external files or GitHub operations.

A recovery card may offer to restore cut controls when the required state remains available. After the operation, inspect the designer and properties. Treat a partial result as partial; preserve the indicated backup before any new action.
editor: Monaco displays and edits modules from the selected project. Its status bar lets you track application of the text to native VBA code.
Open a module and follow its synchronization
Open the module from the VBE or a chat reference. Its tab appears in Monaco. After editing, check synchronization status: text visible in a draft is not necessarily the code executed by the host.
Autocomplete and hover information use VBA analysis and libraries accessible to the project. Block and indentation assistance support typing. Compile the project to validate the result.
Choose the right version after divergence
Examine differences between edited text and current native content.
Apply the Monaco text, subject to revision checks and VBE mode.
Replace edited text with current native content.
Recover local text, then compare it before applying.
Preserve the result in the document

After synchronization succeeds, compile and save the document in the host application. If there is a conflict, preserve the useful draft before reloading another version. Choosing a version in the editor and saving the document are separate steps.
forms: Request creation or development of a form in the chat, then check its design in the VBE.

Our first request describes a small window for calculating amounts before tax, VAT and amounts including tax. The agent chooses the necessary controls and code. You can then request a more compact layout, a different size or a font change in a separate exchange.

For a targeted change, give the form name or attach its reference. Specify the text to display and the relevant element when several controls serve the same purpose. The agent can read available properties before changing them.
Open the form in the native designer. Check labels, dimensions, alignment, tab order and event code. Ask for a property to be read again if the applied value seems different.
Then run the form with your test data. A visible design alone does not validate input conversions or the calculation. Request tests for testable logic separately and check the interactive workflow.
The form created by Luna, running in Excel: 100 before tax at 20% yields 120.00 including tax.
Change a container or a specific property

Identify the page or container when a control belongs to a Frame or MultiPage. Deleting a container can remove its children. Fonts, images and ActiveX controls have their own constraints; discovering a property does not imply it is editable.
To version or restore a form, keep its FRM definition and any FRX resources together. After recovery, check the designer as well as the code.
debug: The chat can assist with compilation, running a procedure and inspecting a break. The selected project and VBE mode determine available actions.

After implementation, ask the agent to compile the project and check its behavior. If it must run a procedure, specify the expected scenario and data to use. The result should identify the procedure actually executed and any diagnostics.

Request a breakpoint on an executable line, then execution of the scenario. Once the breakpoint is reached, ask for useful values or single stepping. Check which procedure and project the observed information belongs to.
Debugging windows may be shared between projects. Reading them remains subject to the conversation’s access scope. Some evaluations call code; the result depends on the actual execution context.
Return to a state that permits editing
Normally allows structural and code changes.
Some operations must wait or are unavailable.
Allows inspection; not all code changes are permitted.
A successful compilation, an executed scenario and a saved document are three separate results. Read the state again after a stop or error before repeating an action.
git-conversion: Convert a VBA project to Git sources
VBAi manages a source package in vba/ and imports it back into an existing host project. This section explains the generated format, the checks applied and what each synchronization preserves.
Macro / repository conversion
VBA sources
manifest.json
UserForm
Encoding
First publication
What VBAi exports
The GitHub window exports components from the selected project, their native attributes and form resources. It does not publish the complete workbook or its data sheets.
To use the project in another application or document, prepare the necessary host objects and libraries. The versioned package provides code; it does not create those dependencies.
The source package produced by VBAi

In the repository, VBAi manages the vba/ subfolder. It contains manifest.json and component files. Other repository files, such as README.md, remain separate. Do not put personal or unrelated files in vba/: this subfolder belongs to the managed source package.

The manifest inventories the package: format version, component names and types, presence of form resources and reference identities. These references indicate required libraries; the manifest does not install them.
Example file
Contents and consequence
vba/manifest.json
Inventory used to understand and validate the package before import.
vba/modCalculTVA.bas
Standard module exported by the VBE, with its attributes.
vba/ClassBudget.cls
Exported class with its attributes; this is not simply text copied from the code window.
vba/frmCalculTVA.frm
Exported form definition and associated code.
vba/frmCalculTVA.frx
Binary resources for the same form, where present. They accompany the .frm.
vba/ThisWorkbook.vba
Visible code from the module linked to the existing workbook; does not create a new workbook.
vba/Feuil1.vba
Visible code from an existing worksheet module; does not create the sheet or its cells.
Why a form sometimes uses two files

The .frm describes the exported form; the .frx preserves binary resources referenced by that definition. Versioning only the .frm when a .frx is required can lose the design or prevent import. Keep both files for the same form in the same change.

A binary resource cannot be merged line by line like VBA. In a conflict, choose a consistent form/resource set, then check the design and properties in the VBE. Comparison reduces certain recognized native storage differences, without arbitrarily converting resources or removing an unknown control.
Do not rename a .frm, its .frx and its manifest entry separately. Names and resource references must remain consistent.
Accents, line endings and attributes

Native VBE export uses the Windows code page. VBAi reads this export strictly and produces UTF-8 text without a BOM and with LF line endings in the repository. A modern editor can therefore read accented comments and strings correctly.

During import, UTF-8 sources are converted back to the VBE code page and native line endings. An unrepresentable character causes refusal before project changes; it is not silently replaced with a question mark.

Attribute lines and export headers carry information the code window does not always show. Edit useful code without removing this metadata, and preserve the package format. A repository containing only pasted text without a manifest is not automatically an importable VBAi package.
Three states to distinguish
State
What it means
VBA open in the host
The code you are currently editing in the VBE. It may not yet be saved in the document file.
Local Git history
Commits in the local repository managed by VBAi. A commit exists here before any upload to GitHub.
Branch on GitHub
Published commits that collaborators can fetch. They do not immediately change VBA that is already open.

VBAi also keeps a reference state from the last synchronization. Comparison checks the live project against this baseline to identify local changes. This distinguishes your uncommitted work from a newly received version.
A commit snapshots the selected sources in local Git. Push publishes the commits. Save in Excel, Word or SOLIDWORKS writes the host document. These three operations do not substitute for one another.
First publication of your existing macro
Start by working on a copy of your document. Save it, verify the right project, unlock it if needed and remain in design mode.
Connect the repository GitHub account in settings. Also configure your commit name and email in Git for Windows if you have not already done so.
Choose a suitable repository and branch. A private repository limits visibility, but you must also check who has access to it.
Link the repository to the project. Linking alone does not publish code or replace the macro.
Compare exported sources. Check modules, classes, forms and references. Remove keys or passwords from the code before publishing: VBAi does not remove them for you.
Select the sources to include, enter a message such as “First version of CalculTVA sources”, then create the local commit.
Click Push to publish the branch. Check GitHub: the vba/ subfolder should show the manifest and expected components.
Also save your document in the application. The commit has not saved sheets, data or the host macro file.

If the remote branch already contains a different VBA package, the first local commit may be refused and require a prior Pull. Do not replace this history with a force push; choose the right repository or deliberately prepare to import the remote contents.
The agent created and published the commit on the example branch. The repository contains the vba/ package, not the complete Excel file.
Import repository code into a macro
Prepare a disposable host document or a backed-up copy. For Excel, create the necessary sheets and document modules with the expected names before import.
Under Tools > References, align the expected libraries. A missing reference blocks capture; different references block import.
Link the branch containing the vba/ package. Preview the import and read file changes.
If the project has local changes since its last baseline, commit them or explicitly handle them before Pull. VBAi refuses to overwrite them silently.
Run Pull and import. VBAi validates sources, prepares native files and preserves a backup before making changes.
Read the result. Open the affected modules and forms, check properties, then compile the project.
Run only tests appropriate to your working copy. Then save the document in the host application.
Import reconstructs code in the chosen project; it does not execute the macro, install libraries, create workbook sheets or automatically save the document.
What VBAi checks during reverse conversion

Before the first write, VBAi prepares the entire package, checks project identity and mode, compares its state with the initially observed state and checks references. Incoming document modules must match host modules already present.
Changed standard modules, classes and forms are replaced or imported according to the package. Document module code is updated in existing objects. Unchanged components are not needlessly replaced.
After application, VBAi reads the actual project again and verifies the result. A completed Git operation is therefore insufficient: the result must match the project actually imported.
The source package does not contain a digital signature for the VBA project. Do not assume that the original macro’s signature is carried with exports or remains valid after code changes.
If import fails or remains uncertain

A native error can occur after some changes. Immediately repeating import could add a second change to a poorly understood state. VBAi preserves the backup and marks recovery as pending rather than reporting success.

Automatic restoration checks that live code still matches the state observed after import. If you changed code since then, or that state could not be read, it may refuse to avoid overwriting your work. This refusal does not mean the backup has disappeared.
Preserve traces and local Git storage, inspect the macro, then use the offered restoration workflow. If manual recovery is needed, work on a copy and keep before/after states.
Where local data lives

The managed local repository is under %LOCALAPPDATA%\VBAi\Git and depends on the saved document path, remote repository and branch. It is a bare repository: VBAi manipulates Git objects without creating a normal working folder beside the macro.
Temporary native export and import files use %LOCALAPPDATA%\VBAi\GitTemporary. The local Git repository is more than a downloadable cache: it may contain unpushed commits and recovery backups.

Moving or renaming the document may require linking again. Do not delete Git storage to “refresh” a list unless you have checked unpublished commits and backups. Private recovery references are not published by normal pushes.
git-connect: Link the document to a repository
Linking associates the saved document with a repository and branch. It prepares Git operations without automatically importing or publishing code.
In VBAi settings, connect the GitHub account used for repositories. This connection is separate from the provider chosen for the chat.
Open GitHub · VBAi for the desired project. In GitHub, find the existing repository and choose Use repository, or enter its reference in GitHub repository.
Check the indicated branch and document, then start linking. Read the result before continuing.
In the illustrated walkthrough, the repository is disposable and the branch is reserved for the example. For your project, explicitly choose the repository and its visibility.
Top of the actual GitHub window: linking the document to its working branch.
Check the repository and branch before linking.
Exports the current project to show its differences from the tracked baseline.
Updates remote references without importing code into the VBE.
Publishes local commits on the linked branch.
Fetches and applies sources after validation and backup.
Opens the recovery workflow for the backed-up state.

Before an initial import, examine remote sources and their references. They can replace the current project’s code. If your goal is to publish a new project, verify that the chosen branch is suitable for this first publication.
Commits use the Git identity configured on the machine. VBAi manages linking and the local repository: you do not need to create a Git directory beside the document.
git-changes: Review and publish changes
The Git changes tab shows differences in the current project. Use it to prepare commit contents before publication.
Commit
Git history
Checkpoint
Restore a module
Prepare the commit
Click Compare and select a file to read its differences.
Check included files. Keep a form’s definition and resources together.
Enter a message, then use Commit selected. Read the result and changes remaining outside the commit.
Click Push when the local selection is ready to publish. Then check the remote branch.
Open in VBE navigates to the component; Restore module replaces its content. Read the command again before activating it.
Initial component selection: the form includes its resources; references are selected separately.
Find a version

In History, select a commit to read its details. Compare lets you examine two revisions without changing the project. An open macro can contain additional edits since the latest commit: use Compare to identify them.
After publication: the dedicated branch has no commits awaiting upload or fetch.
Read the branch name and counters after Push or Fetch.
Create a restore point
In Checkpoints, name the state you want to preserve before a transformation. To return to it, select it and request restoration. Check the restored content in the VBE, then save the document.
A checkpoint supports project recovery. It does not replace publishing commits. If restoration reports a partial state, preserve recovery information before continuing.
git-branches: Switch branches and handle a merge
VBAi branch operations are linked to the open VBA project. Check local changes before an operation that imports another version.
In Branches, Create uses the entered name. Enable Remote branches to display fetched references and use Track to prepare local tracking. Check the active branch in the synchronization bar.
Switching branches also imports their sources into the project. First handle reported local changes; selecting a list row should not be confused with simply browsing history.
Select the branch to merge into the current branch and check the direction of the operation. If there are conflicts, open the corresponding tab.
Select the file and examine local, incoming and common versions.
Choose Keep local, Keep incoming or compose the complete version in the resolution area.
Validate the file resolution; repeat for each conflict.
Finish the merge, then inspect and compile the imported project. Abort merge abandons the current merge workflow.

Use this text takes the complete content, including required attributes. For an FRX resource, choose a version consistent with the associated FRM. After import, check the native design: code comparison does not show every form property.
pull-requests: Prepare and view a pull request
The GitHub panel groups review information for the linked repository and lets you prepare a proposal from your published branch.
Load pull requests, select one, then open Details, Files, Comments or Checks. Check the status bar if a list remains empty: it may be loading or reporting a permissions or connection problem.
Open on GitHub takes you to the review for operations not offered in VBAi.
Publish the source branch commits and check the target branch in the creation form.
Enter the title and description. If a draft is suggested, review the changes and validations it claims.
Check Draft if work still needs completion, then create the pull request.
Keep the returned link and check the review’s files.

For the VAT calculation, state which cases were actually run, their result and the host used. GitHub checks concern the repository; passing them does not replace testing the form in its host application. Creating the review does not automatically import code for other users either.
tests: VBAi Test Explorer discovers project tests, runs a selection and displays results. It does not automatically write scenarios for you.

After creating the form, continue with a separate request: “Can you now add tests to check the calculation and input cases that could cause problems, then run them? Fix what does not work and tell me what was verified.”

The agent can adapt code to make the logic testable. Review these changes as you did the initial implementation. Then check the tests actually discovered and their results; a chat response is not enough to establish execution.
Open Test Explorer for the relevant project and refresh discovery.
Use search, grouping and the results filter to choose your batch. Select a test to open its source or read its details.
If test support is requested, examine the comparison before installing it. This step adds code to the project and preserves a backup.
Tests in the scope currently shown.
Instrumented workflow offered for this selection or scope.
Failing tests in the current results.
Requests a stop between tests without immediately interrupting the current test natively.
Read the result and preserve the report
Wait for the batch to finish, then open details of failures, errors or inconclusive results. Copy or Export preserves the current report. Discovery alone does not mean tests were run.

In the example, an initial batch passes five tests and fails an exact Double comparison. The agent corrects the assertion. A subsequent run remains uncertain and is not counted as successful. After inspection and reopening Excel, a new batch completes with six passes. These results describe separate runs; final success does not erase previous traces.

VBA procedure coverage concerns this test workflow in the macro. It measures neither all C# lines and branches in VBAi nor every form scenario. Supplement it with interactive checks of input, focus and presentation.
Actual chat report: six tests passed after correction. Previous attempts remain identified separately.
updates: Review a proposed version and follow update preparation when a trusted package is available.
Check for updates queries the configured source and shows the version and its notes. Include prereleases broadens the versions offered.

Automatic options control daily checking, downloading and installation after VBA hosts close. Save preserves these preferences; Ignore version and Cancel scheduled update act on the relevant proposal.

The standalone installer is a later project milestone. This interface’s presence does not mean that a signed installer has been published or accepted. The current policy requires an approved publisher before installing a package.
The progress window shows status and any wait for hosts to close. Downloading and file trust use separate validations, including SHA-256 and Authenticode.
A passed deadline does not prove an installation process finished. Do not automatically restart an installation with an uncertain outcome; check traces and the offered state.
support: Find the VBAi version and compose a report that you can review before sending.
About shows the version, host, platform and interface language. Copy technical information prepares this metadata for a support request without copying code, paths or project identifiers.
Links provide access to the repository, documentation and GitHub reporting. Update checking has its own workflow.
The chat’s … menu gives access to About VBAi. The same icons are used by VBAi commands in native menus.
Version, host, platform and language information in About VBAi.
Give a title describing the symptom and explain what you were doing, the expected result and the observed result.
Review the complete preview. Remove any sensitive data you added manually.
Copy or save the report if you want to send it yourself.
Use Send report for the GitHub workflow; the email route opens the offered mail workflow if needed.
The report does not automatically collect VBA, conversations, identifiers or personal paths. Text you enter can contain this information, however: the preview remains your checkpoint.
troubleshooting: Resolve common difficulties
Identify the affected level before repeating an action: loading, account, model, project or synchronization.
Troubleshooting
Loading
Error
Empty list
Synchronization
Symptom and first check
Symptom
What to check
VBAi missing or unable to load
Add-In Manager entry, COM identity and x64 DLL path; a visible menu alone does not prove loading.
Closed panel
